Use pipe-based prompt passing for subagents

Passing prompts as flags is unreliable due to shell escaping issues.
New approach: write prompt to temp file, then pipe to CLI.

- cat /tmp/task-prompt.md | claude --model MODEL -p
- cat /tmp/task-prompt.md | gemini --approval-mode auto_edit
- cat /tmp/task-prompt.md | codex exec --model MODEL -

Tested and verified working with all three providers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Start with open prompt, then drill down with questions

Changed flow:
1. Open with "What are we working on today?" (no AskUserQuestion)
2. User describes intent freely
3. Model acknowledges, then uses AskUserQuestion to drill down
4. Questions adapt to scope (small script vs full product)

Key changes:
- Don't front-load with multiple choice forms
- Let user describe naturally first
- Match questioning depth to project scope
- Skip PRD entirely for tiny things

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Simplify 001-scope-project to outcome-driven approach

Remove rigid 21-phase structure in favor of flexible iterative discovery:

- Define required outcomes (what must be captured)
- Provide questioning principles (how to iterate)
- Let the model adapt naturally to each project

Key changes:
- SKILL.md: 5 simple steps instead of 21 phases
- question-phases.md: Now "Questioning Guide" with principles
- prd-template.md: Flexible template with project-type sections
- README.md: Updated to reflect simpler approach

Philosophy: Keep asking questions until you have everything needed.
No predetermined structure - follow threads naturally.

- 🐛 Bug Fix (root cause analysis)
- 🔒 Security Audit (threat actors, attack surface)
- ⚡ Performance Optimization (bottlenecks, metrics)
- 🔗 Integration/Migration (data flows, cutover)

Changes:
- Add project type + focus area opening questions
- Add phase applicability matrix by project type
- Adapt all 21 phases with project-type-specific questions
- Update PRD template with alternative section framings
- Update README to reflect broader scope

Questions now adapt based on project type (e.g., "user personas"
becomes "threat actors" for security audits).
